messages.text: random q, for a top-down delivery game is A* or Dijkstra better for npc pathing on a tile grid? the tiles have different movement costs (mud slows you down)

A* is usually the better choice when each NPC has a single destination. It uses a heuristic to steer the search toward the goal, so it expands far fewer tiles than Dijkstra, and it handles weighted tiles like mud just fine as long as the heuristic never overestimates the remaining cost. Dijkstra is better when you need distances to many targets at once, for example a flow field that many NPCs share.
ok A* it is. what heuristic should i use if diagonal moves are allowed?

Use octile distance: with dx and dy as the absolute differences, take the larger one plus about 0.41 times the smaller one, scaled by your cheapest tile cost. That keeps it admissible. If you want to stay safe, use the minimum movement cost across all tile types as the scale factor.
